summary: 20 juin : NEUTRAL (VIX 16.41, DXY 100.78). Warsh hawkish debut reshuffles the deck — dollar surging, crypto crushed (BTC -6%, ETH -8%), gold pulled back from $4,463 to $4,195. S&P 7,600+ notches 11th winning week in 12 but equities-vs-everything-else divergence is unsustainable. PCE Thursday is the week's arbiter. Micron earnings (rev +276% YoY) and Russell reconstitution (237 additions) add catalysts.

risks.label: PCE Inflation Thursday — Fed's preferred gauge
risks.detail: May PCE Price Index drops Thursday June 25. Core PCE expected +0.3% MoM / 3.4% YoY. After Warsh's hawkish FOMC (half of officials signal rate hike), a hot PCE print could spike dollar past 102, trigger equity pullback 2-3%, and flush crypto further. The single most important data point of the week.

risks.label: Iran deal collapse risk — 60-day ceasefire fragile
risks.detail: 14-point MOU includes 60-day ceasefire and Strait of Hormuz reopening. IRGC hardliners, Israeli opposition, and provocative incidents could unravel the deal. If Hormuz closes again, oil retests $100+ within days, reigniting inflation and potentially forcing Fed emergency response.

risks.label: Dollar wrecking ball — DXY 100.78 and rising
risks.detail: Warsh's hawkish debut sent DXY to 100.78, strongest since April. Structural headwind for gold, crypto, EM equities, and US multinationals. If DXY breaks 102 (hot PCE or more hawkish signals), expect accelerated outflows from gold, EM, and crypto.

risks.label: VIX complacency — 16.41 well below average
risks.detail: S&P has won 11 of 12 weeks. VIX at 16.41 vs 20 long-term average. This level of complacency historically precedes sharp corrections. A shock event (Iran collapse + hot PCE) could trigger VIX spike to 30+ and 5%+ equity sell-off.

risks.label: Rate hike odds rising — new Fed era under Warsh
risks.detail: 9 of 19 FOMC officials now project at least one rate hike this year (up from 4 in March). Market prices ~25% probability of 25bps hike by September. If realized, first hike since July 2023. Fed put is further away.

risks.label: Micron earnings binary risk — Tuesday after close
risks.detail: MU Q3 FY2026: EPS $20.05, Rev $35B (+276% YoY). Bar extraordinarily high. HBM order slowing, DRAM pricing weakness, or inventory buildout could send MU -10%+ and drag entire AI complex (NVDA, AMD, ASML). Options imply ±8% move.

events.label: Warsh's first FOMC — hawkish surprise reshuffles deck
events.detail: New Fed Chair Kevin Warsh held rates at 5.25-5.50% but revealed half of FOMC members support a rate hike this year. Dollar surged to 100.78, crypto plunged, gold retreated. Fundamental shift: not Powell's Fed anymore. Higher-for-longer framework becomes structural.

events.label: S&P 500 — 11th winning week in 12, above 7,600
events.detail: S&P 500 above 7,600 for first time, logging 23rd ATH of 2026 earlier in June. Nasdaq +2.4%, Russell 2000 +13.2% YTD leader. Rally increasingly broad-based: equal-weight SPX up ~8% vs cap-weight ~11%. Breadth healthy but complacency elevated.

events.label: Russell semi-annual reconstitution — first ever, June 26
events.detail: Historic first semi-annual Russell reconstitution. 237 additions to Russell 2000. Massive index-tracking flows expected Thursday/Friday. Small-cap IWM already YTD leader at +13.2%. Additions tend to rally into reconstitution day.

events.label: Micron joins $1T club — AI memory supercycle
events.detail: Micron crossed $1 trillion market cap in late May. Q3 earnings Tuesday: EPS $20.05 (vs $2.38 year-ago), Rev $35B (+276% YoY). HBM3E demand from hyperscalers transforms MU from cyclical DRAM player to structural AI beneficiary. 25-30% HBM market share.

events.label: FedEx Freight spinoff — first post-separation earnings
events.detail: FedEx reports Monday June 23. First quarterly results since June 1 spinoff of FedEx Freight. Remaining FDX is pure-play express delivery. Bellwether for global trade volumes and e-commerce growth. EPS est $5.92, Rev $24B.

opportunities.label: MU post-earnings — AI memory supercycle play
opportunities.detail: Micron (MU) earnings Tuesday after close. If beat-and-raise: enter post-earnings gap up. 8x forward PE vs Nvidia 35x = best value among AI semi plays. HBM pricing power + $660-$690B hyperscaler spend in 2026. Conditioned entry eliminates binary risk. Stop -7%, TP1 +10%, TP2 +18%.

opportunities.label: IWM — Russell reconstitution catalyst
opportunities.detail: Russell 2000 ETF (IWM) for reconstitution flows + structural small-cap rally. YTD leader +13.2%, 43% projected earnings growth. 237 additions create massive index-fund buying. Entry at market Monday, stop -4%, TP1 +5%, TP2 +8%.

opportunities.label: TLT — contrarian duration play on PCE outcome
opportunities.detail: 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF. Contrarian bet that market overreacts to Warsh's hawkishness. 10Y yield already fell from 4.55% to 4.44% — bonds quietly pricing tighter policy slows growth. Cool PCE triggers sharp rally. Entry ~$85, stop $82, TP1 $89, TP2 $93. Half-position due to binary nature.

opportunities.label: Gold pullback opportunity — structural bull intact
opportunities.detail: Gold at $4,195, down 6% from $4,463 ATH. Pullback driven by dollar surge, not fundamental deterioration. Central bank buying continues at record pace. Expert forecasts $4,300-$4,750. Wait for PCE clarity: cool PCE = buy the dip.

opportunities.label: Value > Growth rotation — energy +21% YTD leader
opportunities.detail: 2026 broadening trade: equal-weight SPX +8% vs cap-weight +11%. Energy (+21% YTD), Materials (+17%), Staples (+15%) lead. Russell 2000 Value +46.3% vs Growth +42.6% trailing 12M. Breadth expansion more durable than mega-cap concentration.

regime_blips.label: NEUTRAL — equities vs everything else divergence
regime_blips.detail: Paradox: S&P 7,600+ (risk-on) but dollar 100.78, crypto crushed, gold retreating (risk-off signals). Stocks price growth while dollar prices tightening. One narrative must break — PCE Thursday is the arbiter. VIX 16.41 complacency deepens the tension.

regime_blips.label: Dollar strength structural under Warsh
regime_blips.detail: DXY at 100.78, strongest since April. Warsh's hawkish stance + rate hike odds create structural dollar bid. Inverse correlation with gold (-0.78), crypto (-0.72), EM (-0.71) all active. Dollar above 102 = next leg down for USD-denominated assets.

regime_blips.label: BTC/SPY decorrelation — crypto now rate-sensitive
regime_blips.detail: BTC/SPY 60-day correlation dropped from 0.72 to 0.45. Crypto transitioning from risk-on asset to rate-sensitive asset under Warsh's Fed. BTC now trades more like gold — inversely with dollar. Cannot rely on crypto to rally alongside equities anymore.

regime_blips.label: Yield curve de-inverting — 2s/10s at -36bps
regime_blips.detail: 2s/10s spread narrowed from -90bps to -36bps. Past 'maximum inversion' phase, potentially entering more dangerous 'steepening' phase that historically precedes recessions. HY spreads still tight (~360bps) — no credit stress yet.

regime_blips.label: AI capex supercycle intact — $660-690B spend 2026
regime_blips.detail: Hyperscaler AI capex at $660-690B in 2026. Micron's +276% revenue growth confirms structural HBM shortage. Semis remain the strongest thematic trade despite dollar headwind. Nasdaq +2.4% weekly outperforms.
